# Muse Fanqie download tools

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

`fanqie_download_info` checks the official complete directory for one or more books. `fanqie_download` downloads all currently published chapters into UTF-8 TXT files in the initiating session workspace. Pass decimal string IDs or official `https://fanqienovel.com/page/<book-id>` links in `bookIds`. The result includes the current official title, declared and downloaded chapter counts, absolute file paths, SHA-256 and per-chapter receipts. For an ongoing book, `complete` means its current published directory; it does not mean the author has finished the novel. Directory inspection alone never claims a verified download.

The independent local Python engine uses normal anonymous device registration and read endpoints. Devices and negotiated keys stay in memory and are not copied from the reference application, published or logged. The closed-source reference application is not shipped. MIT-licensed protocol primitives retain their notices and pinned source records in `SOURCE.json`. The engine refuses paid/VIP or other authorization-required content, missing or mismatched chapters, previews, undecoded font characters and undersized text. Every book must pass before the batch directory is published; a failure or cancellation removes all newly staged files and preserves existing downloads.

Desktop presets mount the tools and reuse the packaged Hongguo Python/PyCryptodome runtime. No additional Java service, external downloader or TOS credential is needed. An independent profile can install the package and apply `cordis.patch.yml` with `MUSE_FANQIE_PYTHON_PATH`, or configure `pythonExecutable` directly. Python must include PyCryptodome and a functioning TLS certificate store. Unconfigured runtime fails at the first call. Loading the plugin performs no network request. Model tools use the Host subprocess service; unload aborts and waits for active engines and cleanup.

Configuration accepts `pythonExecutable` (empty by default), `requestTimeoutMs` (30000), `callTimeoutMs` (1800000), `graceMs` (1000), `maxBooks` (10), `batchSize` (10), `maxResponseBytes` (16 MiB), `maxChapterBytes` (2 MiB), `maxBookBytes` (128 MiB), and `maxOutputBytes` (16 MiB). Numeric limits must be positive safe integers. There is no chapter-count cap. `outputDir` defaults to `downloads/fanqie` and must stay inside the session workspace without symlink directories. Each successful batch receives a new directory and never overwrites an older book. HTTP redirects are refused; the engine contacts only its fixed official registration and reading hosts.

Run `node --test tests/*.test.js` and `<python> -I -B tests/engine_test.py` for offline behavior checks. `node scripts/pack.mjs --out <absolute-directory>` creates the npm archive. With the Host and native addon built, set `MUSE_FANQIE_LIVE_BOOK_IDS` to comma-separated authorized free-book IDs and `MUSE_FANQIE_PYTHON_PATH` to the Python path, then run `node --test tests/live.test.js` for real-source qualification. It skips unless explicitly enabled. Platform package validation belongs to the final Muse release; a source-level download check does not establish that a Windows or Mac installer works.
